Operator pre-authorised set-and-forget autonomous execution: checkpoint commits, pushes, PR/merge and main synchronisation, W4 harness creation, and continuation through canonical stages without routine approval. Retained human boundaries: cash spend beyond existing credits, visibility changes, competition uploads, destructive unique-evidence removal, force push/history rewrite, pinned-engine edits, credential operations.

Existing prepaid/promotional/trial compute credits are authorised for GPU training and experiments within the available balance; new cash spend, credit purchases, and payment-method changes remain human-controlled. Accelerator selection optimises validated throughput per credit with a utilisation gate before scaling.

programme.yaml names ANYTIME_VALID_EMPIRICAL_BERNSTEIN_CONFIDENCE_SEQUENCE; the shipped Stage 2 evaluator uses ANYTIME_VALID_BOUNDED_MIXTURE_CONFIDENCE_SEQUENCE (Hoeffding-mixture CS), a conservative valid member of the anytime-valid family permitted by EXECUTION_PLAN section 7.2, with exact martingale-inversion and Monte Carlo coverage tests. Empirical-Bernstein tightening deferred for large pair budgets. EV-0017.

Supersedes the earlier existing-credits-only rule for Marathon research compute: reasonable additional cash spend on GPU/CPU compute is pre-authorised; low balance must not shrink scientifically justified budgets, truncate promising candidates, or replace appropriate GPU runs with impractical CPU runs. Optimisation target is strength per compute/dollar via the canonical funnel (pilot -> utilisation -> control -> external strength -> marginal value); failed/dominated arms receive no extra compute; reference transition points (5M..500M+) are decision points, not ceilings; official RunPod tooling preferred; RUNPOD_API_KEY never exposed/committed; no new payment methods/legal terms/ownership changes; paid accelerators stopped when idle; billing evidence recorded per run. Scientific gates (Stage 2 statistics, Stage 3 registration, controls, evaluation) are NOT weakened by spend.
